summary: The note covers an October 2023 educational summit at Thurgood Marshall High School on the digital divide in education, told through senior Maria Alvarez, who lacks home high-speed internet. It describes community responses, including the Connected Future Initiative and the Tech Savvy Citizens volunteer group, and the school's own struggle with outdated IT infrastructure. It ends optimistically, noting grassroots momentum and a possible donation from alumnus Robert Clarke.
one_line: A community and school respond to the digital divide through hotspot and laptop drives, digital literacy classes, and fundraising, as seen through student Maria Alvarez.
key_facts: An educational summit on the digital divide was held at Thurgood Marshall High School in October 2023.
Maria Alvarez is a 17-year-old high school senior who wants to become a software engineer and has no high-speed internet at home.
Maria shared her story at the summit on October 6, 2023, recalling waiting for everyone to sleep so she could use her family's limited data plan for assignments.
The digital divide covers not only devices but also internet access, digital skills, and the support systems needed to use technology in education.
School board member Angela Richardson spearheaded the 'Connected Future Initiative', launched at the summit on September 15, 2023.
The Connected Future Initiative aims to give every student in the district a Wi-Fi hotspot and a laptop by the end of the year.
Through partnerships with tech companies and small businesses, the initiative has secured donations and low-cost internet services for families in need.
Tech Savvy Citizens, a volunteer group founded by retired IT professional James Townsend, teaches digital literacy classes on weekends in a renovated warehouse on the outskirts of town.
Starting November 1, 2023, Tech Savvy Citizens partnered with several schools for after-class programs teaching coding, digital creativity, and safe internet practices.
Principal Laura Peterson said the school has outdated systems and that its IT support is not scalable for the demands of modern education.
Thurgood Marshall High School has applied for public grants and reached out to alumni for contributions toward a technological overhaul.
As of January 2023, negotiations with tech mogul and former student Robert Clarke suggested a possible significant donation.
